hook.en: Neck and spine glides applied along the facet joint while the patient moves actively (SNAG) or in gentle oscillation (NAG).
hook.ur: NAGs, SNAGs aur Self-SNAGs spinal mobilization ke tareeqay hain jin mein joint ki glide ko passive ya active movement ke sath combine kiya jata hai.

goal.en: By the end, you'll know what Mulligan NAGs, SNAGs & Self-SNAGs is, when it's safe and useful, how to apply it step by step — and how to prove it worked. (3 checks along the way.)
goal.ur: End tak aap jaan jayenge ke Mulligan NAGs, SNAGs & Self-SNAGs kya hai, kab safe aur faida-mand hai, qadam ba qadam kaise apply hoti hai — aur kaise prove karein ke kaam kiya. (Raste mein 3 checks.)

text.en: SNAG means Sustained Natural Apophyseal Glide: you glide one vertebra along the angle of its facet joint while the patient actively moves the painful way. NAG means Natural Apophyseal Glide, applied as a gentle oscillating glide, often to find the right direction. Self-SNAGs let the patient apply the glide themselves with a towel or hands.
text.ur: Yeh techniques spinal facet joints ki direction mein glide ko movement ke sath combine karti hain. Self-SNAG mein patient ko safe tareeqay se khud movement karna sikhaya ja sakta hai.

text.en: A facet joint is like a ramp. If you push the vertebra up the ramp's own slope while the neck turns, the movement runs smoothly; if you push across it, the movement jams.
text.ur: Facet joint ek dhalaan (ramp) jaisa hai. Agar neck ghumate waqt vertebra ko ramp ki apni dhalaan ke saath upar dhakelein to movement smooth hoti hai; agar dhalaan ke aar-paar dhakelein to movement atak jati hai.

text.en:
Three ideas carry this whole technique:
**1.** Glide along the facet plane, roughly toward the patient's eyes in the neck, while the patient moves.
**2.** The movement must be pain-free and clearly better at once (the same PILL idea as other Mulligan techniques).
**3.** Because it is near the neck, careful screening for blood-vessel and neurological problems comes first.
text.ur: In ka maqsad patient ki participation ke sath pain-free spinal movement behtar karna hai. Self-SNAG safe tareeqay se sikhaya jaye to manual concept ko home strategy mein badal sakta hai. Response ko foran movement ki tabdeeli aur symptoms ke rawaiye se judge karna chahiye.

text.en:
So when does **Mulligan NAGs, SNAGs & Self-SNAGs** make sense?
• Painful neck rotation or flexion where a segment is tender.
• Headaches arising from the upper neck that are reproduced by neck movement.
• Stiff upper-back movements in sitting.
text.ur: Mechanical spinal pain; dard ke sath movement restriction; screening ke baad kuch selected headache ya cervicogenic presentations.

text.en:
And just as important — when you should NOT use it, or should stop:
• Dizziness, visual disturbance, difficulty speaking or swallowing, or any neurological sign.
• Fracture, instability, infection or unexplained severe pain.
• No instant pain-free improvement.
text.ur:
Upper cervical symptoms, chakkar, ya vascular ya ligament-related disorder ki history ho to khaas ehtiyat aur munasib screening zaroori hai.
Cervical arterial pathology ka shak, instability, fracture, acute myelopathy, ya barhta hua neurological deficit.
Technique ka naam yaad hona safe application ke barabar nahi. Movement force karna, feedback ignore karna, unsuitable presentation mein use karna aur retest skip karna aam ghaltiyan hain. Dizziness, nayi neurological symptoms, unusual severe pain ya worsening symptoms hon to rok kar appropriate assessment karein.

title.en: How to do it — 6 steps, each with its reason
title.ur: Kaise karein — 6 qadam, har ek ki wajah ke saath

steps.title: Screen for neck red flags
steps.detail: Check for dizziness, visual change, previous neck injury, and neurological symptoms.

steps.title: Find the painful movement
steps.detail: Example: right rotation is painful at 40 degrees.

steps.title: Contact the vertebra
steps.detail: In sitting, place your thumb pads on the side of the painful vertebra's joint, with support behind your thumb.

steps.title: Apply the glide
steps.detail: Glide gently along the facet plane toward the patient's eyes.

steps.title: Ask the patient to move
steps.detail: They turn through the previously painful range while you hold the glide. It should feel easy and pain-free.

steps.title: Repeat and retest
steps.detail: Repeat 6-10 times. Retest rotation. Teach a self-SNAG if effective.

beats.ur:
1. Limited spinal movement identify karein.
2. Mutaliqa segment par intended direction mein glide dein.
3. SNAG mein glide maintain karte hue patient se active movement karwayein.
4. Sirf us surat mein repeat karein jab movement comfortable rahe aur behtari ho.
5. Self-SNAG tabhi sikhayein jab patient direction ko mehfooz tareeqay se dohra sake.

question.en: Imagine the patient is in front of you. What do you do FIRST?
question.ur: Farz karein patient aap ke saamne hai. Aap SAB SE PEHLE kya karenge?

text.en: How much? Typical teaching range: 6-10 repetitions, 2-3 sets. Stay pain-free. Stop if no instant improvement.
text.ur: Aksar ek set mein 6–10 repetitions istemal ki jati hain, lekin sets ki tadaad response ke mutabiq hoti hai. Home self-SNAG ki dose conservative aur symptoms ke mutabiq honi chahiye.

beats.patient: David, 50, desk worker, neck pain turning to the left to check traffic.
beats.assessment: Left rotation is painful at 45 degrees. Screening is clear.
beats.treatment: You apply a SNAG at the left C5-6 facet while he turns slowly left. The movement becomes pain-free through the range, so he repeats 8 times, three sets.
beats.reassess: Rotation reaches 65 degrees with minimal pain. You teach a towel self-SNAG for home and review in a week.
beats.ur:
Ek misal se poora clinical flow dekhein:
Farz karein neck ghumane mein takleef hai. Assessment aur screening ke baad therapist glide ke sath movement ka response check karta hai. Agar movement comfortable na ho, to technique ko force nahi karta. Yeh fictional example hai, patient-specific prescription nahi.

text.en:
The mistakes I see most often:
• Pushing straight forward instead of along the facet plane.
• Ignoring dizziness or neurological symptoms.
• Continuing when pain does not drop.
text.ur:

• Pushing straight forward instead of along the facet plane.
• Ignoring dizziness or neurological symptoms.
• Continuing when pain does not drop.

text.en: Small studies suggest short-term improvement in neck pain and headache, but evidence is limited and the effect over time is uncertain.
text.ur: Sirf therapist ke hand ke neeche joint feel ko outcome na banayein. Patient ki active movement, symptoms aur function compare karein. Isay guaranteed long-term structural change ke taur par present na karein; English chapter ki evidence summary ke mutabiq balanced explanation dein.
